crypto_call_justification: The project does not implement cryptographic primitives itself. It uses dedicated FLOSS implementations including Node.js Web Crypto, PKI.js, ASN1.js, and node-forge. Project code adds policy enforcement, validation, resource limits, and typed interfaces around those implementations.
crypto_floss_justification:
All cryptographic functionality is implemented using FLOSS runtime and dependencies. The complete dependency set and licenses are publicly inspectable through package.json and package-lock.json:
https://github.com/udid-tools/core/blob/main/package.json
crypto_keylength_justification:
Signing is restricted to RSA keys of at least 2048 bits. Smaller signing keys are always rejected and cannot be enabled through configuration:
https://udid-tools.github.io/core/reference/capability-matrix/
crypto_password_storage_justification: The library does not authenticate external users and does not store passwords. A supplied PKCS#12 passphrase is used only to decode caller-provided signing material and is never persisted or returned.
crypto_pfs_justification: The library performs offline profile signing and signature verification. It does not implement network transport, session establishment, or a key-agreement protocol, so perfect forward secrecy is not applicable.
crypto_published_justification: The beta cryptographic profile uses publicly specified and reviewed standards: CMS/PKCS#7 SignedData, PKCS#12, X.509, RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signatures, and SHA-256. Unsupported algorithms are rejected.
crypto_random_justification: The library does not generate cryptographic keys or protocol nonces. Signing keys and certificates are supplied explicitly by the caller. Automatically generated profile UUIDs use Node.js crypto.randomUUID.
crypto_weaknesses_justification:
Profile signing is restricted to RSA keys of at least 2048 bits with SHA-256. RSA/SHA-1 is accepted only when verifying legacy Apple Profile Service responses for documented interoperability; the library never generates SHA-1 signatures and does not treat successful legacy verification as trust-chain validation.
https://udid-tools.github.io/core/reference/capability-matrix/
crypto_working_justification:
Generated CMS signatures use RSA with SHA-256. The allow-list rejects MD4, MD5, single DES, RC4, and other unsupported algorithms. RSA/SHA-1 support is limited to verification of legacy Apple Profile Service responses and is not used for generated signatures.
https://udid-tools.github.io/core/reference/capability-matrix/
delivery_mitm_justification: Source, documentation, npm packages, GitHub Packages, and release artifacts are delivered over HTTPS. npm releases use provenance and GitHub OIDC trusted publishing.
delivery_unsigned_justification: The project never retrieves a cryptographic hash over unsecured HTTP. Release artifacts remain inside the protected GitHub Actions workflow, are checked with SHA-256, and are published with npm provenance and GitHub attestations.

know_common_errors_justification:
The primary developer addresses common vulnerability classes relevant to this library, including malicious XML/ASN.1 input, entity expansion, parser depth and size exhaustion, unsafe object keys, signature bypass, algorithm confusion, untrusted certificate chains, secret leakage, timing-sensitive challenge comparison, and supply-chain compromise.

https://github.com/udid-tools/core/blob/main/THREAT_MODEL.md
know_secure_design_justification:
The primary developer applies secure-design principles including least privilege, explicit trust boundaries, fail-closed validation, limited attack surface, bounded resource use, sanitized failures, and no implicit filesystem, network, environment, or logging access.

The design and threat analysis are documented here:
https://github.com/udid-tools/core/blob/main/THREAT_MODEL.md
https://github.com/udid-tools/core/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
